name: @yapweijun1996/kb-mcp

tools.name: kb_skill_route
tools.description: Deterministically route a user message to the best Codex/Kb MCP skill workflow. Returns top skill candidates, intent, confidence, suggested tools, required fields, missing fields, extracted hints, and the next action. Use this before choosing a specialized workflow when the user asks for life ledger, research, job search, memory, GitHub/code, news, deployment, or spreadsheet work. How to read the result: `needs_user_input: true` means the top route is confident (≥0.6) but required fields are missing — ask the user for exactly those fields. `route_uncertain: true` means the top route's confidence is below 0.6 — sanity-check the route against the message before committing to its workflow (uncertain ≠ wrong, but do not ask the user for a weak route's missing fields). A top route of `think-before-action` (source `fallback`) means no skill matched strongly enough: handle the task with normal planning instead of forcing a skill. When an optional KB-backed registry is requested, `skill_registry.status` reports loaded, truncated, partial, or unavailable; built-in routing remains available when registry fetches fail.

user_message.description: Raw user message to classify and route.

available_skills.description: Optional list of currently available skill ids. If omitted, built-in route confidence is not penalized.

skill_run_id.description: Optional opaque Skill discovery journey id returned by a previous Skill tool call.

declared_agent.description: Optional declared telemetry label such as codex, claude, or gemini; never used for authorization.

client_instance_id.description: Optional caller instance label. KB-MCP stores only a SHA-256 hash for telemetry.

current_date.description: Current local date for resolving today/now in YYYY-MM-DD.

known_personal_ledger_kb_id.description: Known personal life ledger KB uuid, if already resolved.

skill_registry_kb_id.description: Optional KB uuid containing registered skills as kbcid='agent.skill' and metadata.kind='skill'.

skill_registry_limit.description: Maximum total registry skill items to load from skill_registry_kb_id. Default 100; fetched in deterministic pages of at most 100. The result reports truncation when more items exist.

max_routes.description: Max route candidates to return. Default 3.

tools.name: kb_skill_register
tools.description: Create or update one KB-backed Skill Registry route as a normal KB item using kbcid='agent.skill' and metadata.kind='skill'. It checks the exact stable skill_id and returns conflicting candidates before creating a new canonical item.

kb_id.description: Target Skill Registry knowledge base uuid.

intent.description: Short routing intent/category for this skill.

description.description: What this skill should be used for.

keywords.description: Words/phrases that should route to this skill.

triggers.description: Alternative trigger phrases. Router also understands this field.

suggested_tools.description: MCP tools or connectors commonly needed by this skill.

tools.description: Alias for suggested_tools, kept for registry compatibility.

required_fields.description: Fields an agent should collect before using the skill.

next_action.description: Practical next action shown by kb_skill_route.

reason.description: Human-readable route reason shown by kb_skill_route.

enabled.description: Whether kb_skill_route should use this route. Defaults true.

priority.description: Optional route priority from -10 to 10. Higher gets a small routing boost.

owner.description: Optional owner/team/person responsible for the skill route.

role.description: Optional role namespace, e.g. "data-engineer". Used only to narrow which skills are scored when a caller routes with a role; it never hides a skill, because routing falls back across every role when the in-role pass finds nothing confident.

role_contract.description: Optional temporary role contract selected by kb_agent_context when this skill wins routing. It is lower-priority guidance and cannot override system, repository, safety, or user instructions.

source.description: Optional provenance tag or source path.

metadata.description: Additional metadata to merge before required Skill Registry fields.

body.description: Full SKILL.md playbook (markdown): when, how, steps, examples. Stored as the item content and embedded for search. Returned verbatim by kb_skill_get / kb_skill_export. When omitted, a compact field summary is generated for back-compat.

run.description: Entrypoint the agent runs after materializing files, e.g. 'node scripts/run.mjs'. Stored in metadata.run and returned by kb_skill_export. API keys must come from the agent's host env, never embedded in files.

content.description: File body. Plain text for utf8; base64 string for binary.

files.description: Attached skill files (e.g. .mjs scripts, package.json). Stored in metadata.files with a sha256 per file; kb_skill_export returns them runnable. kb-mcp does NOT execute them — the agent materializes the files and runs them in its own runtime. Total content capped at ~512 KB.

update_item_id.description: Existing registry item id to update instead of creating a new item.

force_create.description: Legacy compatibility flag. It never bypasses an exact same-skill_id conflict; use update_item_id after review.

tools.name: kb_skill_search
tools.description: Search KB-backed Skill Registry routes stored as kbcid='agent.skill' and metadata.kind='skill'. Returns skill_ref values for kb_skill_get or kb_skill_register update_item_id flows.

query.description: Natural-language skill need or skill id to search for.

skill_run_id.description: Optional opaque Skill discovery journey id returned by kb_skill_route or kb_skill_search.

declared_agent.description: Optional declared telemetry label; never used for authorization.

client_instance_id.description: Optional caller instance label. KB-MCP stores only a SHA-256 hash.

kb_ids.description: Optional KB shortlist. Omit to search every visible KB.

strategy.description: Retrieval strategy. Defaults to hybrid; auto uses bounded BM25 then Hybrid fallback.

role.description: Optional role filter applied after retrieval, matched case-insensitively against metadata.role. Use it to search within one role's skills; omit it to search every role.

limit.description: Max skills to return after filtering. Default 10.

tools.name: kb_skill_get
tools.description: Fetch one full Skill Registry definition by skill_ref from kb_skill_search. This is read-only and validates metadata.kind='skill'.

skill_ref.description: Opaque skill ref returned by kb_skill_search, formatted '<kb_uuid>:<item_uuid>'.

skill_run_id.description: Optional Skill discovery journey id from kb_skill_route/kb_skill_search.

declared_agent.description: Optional declared telemetry label; never used for authorization.

client_instance_id.description: Optional caller instance label. KB-MCP stores only a SHA-256 hash.

tools.name: kb_skill_export
tools.description: Export one skill as a runnable bundle for the AGENT'S OWN runtime to execute. kb-mcp does NOT run the code — it returns the SKILL.md `body`, the `run` entrypoint, and every attached file as { path, encoding, bytes, sha256, content }. The agent materializes the files to a temp dir and runs `run` itself (e.g. `node scripts/run.mjs`). Each file's sha256 is recomputed on export and compared to the stored hash so tampering is visible (`integrity_ok`). API keys are never in the bundle — supply them from the agent's host env per the body's instructions.

skill_ref.description: Opaque skill ref returned by kb_skill_search, formatted '<kb_uuid>:<item_uuid>'.

skill_run_id.description: Optional Skill discovery journey id from kb_skill_route/kb_skill_search.

declared_agent.description: Optional declared telemetry label; never used for authorization.

client_instance_id.description: Optional caller instance label. KB-MCP stores only a SHA-256 hash.

tools.name: kb_skill_feedback
tools.description: Record a bounded Level 1 Agent declaration about one existing Skill discovery journey. Use only with skill_run_id returned by kb_skill_route/kb_skill_search/get/export. This is observational feedback: it does NOT verify task success, change Skill utility, change Skill ranking, or grant any permission. For target_kind='skill', the skill_id must be a candidate from that journey and must have actually been read or exported. The server derives Agent/tenant/scope from the authenticated MCP service and locked parent run.

skill_run_id.description: Opaque Skill discovery journey id returned by a Skill tool.

feedback_signal.description: Declared observation only; it never becomes verified success/failure credit in Gate A.4.2a.

target_kind.description: 'run' comments on the whole journey and has no skill_id. 'skill' names one evidenced candidate Skill.

skill_id.description: Required only when target_kind='skill'; must be a Skill evidenced in this Skill run.

reason_text.description: Optional bounded note. KB-MCP/KB-API deterministically redact obvious secrets and identifiers before storage.

supersedes_event_id.description: Optional prior feedback event from the same Skill run/source/target that this event corrects; history remains append-only.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry key. It is sent only as a request header and stored as a SHA-256 hash.

tools.name: kb_skill_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete one skill from the Skill Registry by skill_ref. This is the safe delete for the kb_skill_* family: it first fetches the item and refuses unless metadata.kind='skill', so it can never nuke a non-skill item the way the generic kb_delete_item could. Hard delete — the skill, its embedding, and its attached file bundle (stored in metadata.files) go immediately and cannot be recovered. Any chunked child rows are removed by the DB's ON DELETE CASCADE.

skill_ref.description: Opaque skill ref returned by kb_skill_search, formatted '<kb_uuid>:<item_uuid>'.

tools.name: kb_list
tools.description: List knowledge bases on the server, with item_count per KB, newest first by default. Call this first when the user references a KB by name and you need its uuid. Returns a bounded page (default 20) — use search to jump straight to a known KB instead of paging through everything. If the list is empty, tell the user KBs are created by the operator via /admin — do not try to create one yourself.

sort.description: Sort field (default created_at). `updated_at` is the KB RECORD's own last edit (name/description/visibility/etc.) — it does NOT change when an item inside the KB is added or edited. To find the most recently ACTIVE knowledge base, sort by `last_item_updated_at` instead (max(items.updated_at), null for an empty KB).

tools.name: kb_create
tools.description: Create a new knowledge base. Returns the new KB row including its uuid. visibility controls who can read the KB: 'user' = owner only, 'company' = same company, 'master' = same master, 'global' = anyone authenticated.

visibility.description: Access scope. Default: 'global' for master-scope keys, 'user' otherwise. Only master-scope keys may set 'global'.

schema_type.description: Domain vocabulary template. When set, entity_type values on new items are validated against the schema's vocabulary and warnings are returned for unrecognised types. 'custom' disables validation.

idempotency_key.description: Stable caller-owned key for retrying this exact create after an ambiguous failure. Reuse it only for the same request.

tools.name: kb_get
tools.description: Fetch one knowledge base by uuid. Returns the full KB row including item_count.

kb_id.description: Knowledge base uuid (from kb_list or kb_create)

tools.name: kb_update
tools.description: Partially update a knowledge base (PATCH). Only include fields you want to change. Three-state contract: omit = keep, null = clear (description only), value = update. metadata is replaced wholesale — send the full object you want stored.

description.description: New description. Pass null to clear.

schema_type.description: Domain vocabulary template. Pass null to clear.

tools.name: kb_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a knowledge base and ALL its items (hard delete, cascades). This cannot be undone. Confirm the kb_id with kb_list or kb_get before calling.

tools.name: kb_add_item
tools.description: Insert one knowledge item into a specific KB. The server embeds the item synchronously; expect ~tens of ms to first response after model warm-up. Both title and content are included in the embedding text, so a descriptive title materially improves future retrieval for this item. Set `kbcid` to tag the item with a server-indexed category — the same string can later be passed to kb_search_all's `kbcid` filter for cross-KB routing. Optionally pass `labels` to self-classify the item at write time: `subject` = who it is ABOUT (self/family/external/agent), `assertion` = the kind of claim (self_fact/external_research/reference/event/skill/preference), `confidence` = how sure (confirmed/verified/inferred/recommendation). All three are optional and the server fills the rest by rules/LLM. E.g. a confirmed personal fact about the user → { subject:'self', assertion:'self_fact', confidence:'confirmed' }; a job lead you researched → { subject:'external', assertion:'external_research', confidence:'verified' }; your own reusable runbook → { subject:'agent', assertion:'skill' }.

title.description: Short item title — included in the embedding text

content.description: Full item body — included in the embedding text

kbcid.description: Optional server-indexed category id (1-64 chars, lowercase a-z 0-9 . _ -). Matches the filter accepted by kb_search_all. Examples: 'agrun.runtime', 'globe3-cfm-fixes', 'infra.readurl'. Omit for uncategorised.

entity_type.description: Open taxonomy. Reserved canonical types (meeting, event, decision, requirement, action_item, project, person, organization, task, commit, test_result) require versioned metadata; see the metadata field for all required fields and an event example. For an ordinary feedback or reference item, omit entity_type or use an appropriate custom type such as feedback, bug or fact. Do not invent canonical metadata to satisfy validation.

conditions.description: Optional applicability conditions. Each condition is {key, op, value}. Supported ops: = != >= <= > < in nin. Example: [{"key":"python_version","op":">=","value":"3.10"},{"key":"plan","op":"=","value":"enterprise"}]. Stored as-is (JSONB). Agent reads conditions and decides applicability at query time.

share_level.description: Explicit item share tier. Omit for the conservative 'user' default; the server never infers a higher tier.

source.description: Optional provenance tag — free-form string, not required to be a URL. Examples: 'https://…', 'file:///…', 'chat:session-2026-04-20', 'manual'.

image_url.description: Optional image URL or data: URI stored with the item. Not embedded for search.

metadata.description: For a reserved canonical entity_type, metadata is required: entity_schema_version, canonical_key, status, source_document_id. entity_schema_version must be 1; canonical_key is a stable identifier without spaces; source_document_id identifies the supporting source and is separate from the item's source field. status must be one of draft, planned, confirmed, completed, cancelled, unknown. Additional required fields — meeting: event_date, timezone, participants, project, organization; event: event_date, timezone, participants; task: ticket; commit: commit_sha; test_result: test_key, outcome. event_date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD calendar date; timezone uses an IANA-style name; participants is an array of strings (an empty array is accepted). ticket and test_key must not contain spaces; commit_sha is a 7–64 digit hexadecimal Git object id. outcome must be one of passed, failed, skipped, blocked, unknown. Complete event example (replace illustrative values with source-backed values): {"entity_schema_version":1,"canonical_key":"example:record","status":"confirmed","source_document_id":"example-source-document","event_date":"2026-09-27","timezone":"Asia/Singapore","participants":[]}. Other metadata keys remain supported. For non-canonical types, metadata is optional free-form JSON. Never fabricate a source, date, participant or identity.

subject.description: Who the item is ABOUT: 'self' (the user), 'family', 'external' (companies/jobs/other people/docs), 'agent' (the agent's own skills/runbooks).

assertion.description: Nature of the claim: 'self_fact' (confirmed fact about self/family), 'external_research' (research on the outside world, e.g. job leads), 'reference' (docs/schemas/code), 'event' (a dated occurrence), 'skill' (reusable skill/runbook), 'preference' (a user preference).

labels.description: Optional structured semantic labels to self-classify this item at write time. All sub-fields optional; the server fills the rest by rules/LLM. Do NOT send provenance or version — the server stamps by='agent' and v itself. E.g. a personal fact about the user → { subject:'self', assertion:'self_fact', confidence:'confirmed' }.

upsert_if_similar.description: Opt-in atomic dedup threshold (cosine score 0-1). The REST API updates the nearest standalone item in this KB when its score meets the threshold; otherwise it creates. Omit to always create. Use a conservative high threshold because a false match overwrites data.

idempotency_key.description: Stable identity for one logical write. Generate once and reuse the exact value only for retries after an ambiguous timeout/502.

tools.name: kb_ingest_document
tools.description: Ingest one long document into a KB, letting the server split it into embeddable chunks. Use this instead of kb_add_item whenever the body is more than a few paragraphs (roughly > 1800 chars): a single embedding silently truncates at the model's 512-token window, so a long document added via kb_add_item loses everything past the cut. This tool turns on the server's auto_chunk path by default — content over the threshold is split into sibling chunks under one parent item, each embedded separately, and search can later auto-merge them back with kb_search(include_parent: true). Short documents pass straight through as a single item. Returns the parent `item`, total `chunk_total`, and a compact `children` summary (id + chunk_index per chunk).

title.description: Document title — included in every chunk's embedding text

content.description: Full document body. Long content is split server-side.

kbcid.description: Optional server-indexed category id, applied to every chunk. Same filter as kb_search_all.

share_level.description: Explicit tier applied to the parent and every chunk. Omit for the conservative 'user' default.

source.description: Optional provenance tag (URL, file path, etc.), copied to every chunk.

image_url.description: Optional image URL or data: URI stored with the parent. Not embedded.

metadata.description: Optional free-form JSON metadata copied to every chunk (server appends chunk_index/chunk_total).

max_chars.description: Optional explicit chunk size in chars (server default 1500 when auto-chunking). Supplying this forces explicit chunking regardless of length.

overlap.description: Optional chunk overlap in chars (server default 200). Only used with max_chars.

auto_chunk.description: Whether to let the server split long content. Default true. Set false to force a single item (will truncate at the embedding window if content is long).

idempotency_key.description: Stable identity for this document write. Reuse the exact value only when retrying an ambiguous outcome.

tools.name: kb_bulk_add_item
tools.description: Insert many knowledge items into one KB in a single call. Use this when you have a list of short, already-split items to ingest (e.g. FAQ pairs, structured records) — it saves the per-item round-trip of calling kb_add_item in a loop. For a single long document that still needs splitting, use kb_ingest_document instead; for one short item, kb_add_item. Bulk add does NOT chunk, so each item's content must be <= 1800 chars (the embedding window); a longer item is rejected into `failed` (never silently truncated) — split it first or use kb_ingest_document. Writes run with bounded concurrency and partial-failure semantics: one bad item never aborts the batch. Returns `created` (the inserted rows), `failed` (index + error per rejected item), and a `summary` count. Each item is embedded synchronously, so very large batches take proportionally longer; prefer chunks of a few hundred items.

kb_id.description: Target knowledge base uuid (from kb_list). Applies to every item.

items.description: 1-500 items to insert. Each has the same shape as kb_add_item's body.

concurrency.description: Parallel writes (default 3, max 10). Embedding is synchronous server-side, so high concurrency increases server load without much wall-clock gain.

tools.name: kb_search
tools.description:
Default compact output contains bounded previews and exact references; use response_mode=full for the full rows described below. Raw semantic search inside one KB. The default is semantic hybrid search; set mode=relation_aware for canonical entity filters first, bounded graph expansion, and restricted canonical-only fallback. Prefer kb_answer for normal question-answer retrieval from a known KB because it already returns citations, full parent content, graph neighbours, and a confidence flag in one call. Use kb_search when you intentionally need raw ranked hits for inspection, debugging, routing, or a custom workflow. Returns the top items ranked by cosine similarity in [0, 1] (higher = closer). Use the score to decide whether the top hit is a real answer or just the closest noise, then verify rather than paraphrase a low-confidence hit. Treat < 0.4 as probable noise, but calibrate against the active model — high-band models (bge-m3, e5) score even unrelated content 0.6–0.8, so verify content rather than trusting scores.

Set `include_parent: true` to get full parent documents instead of raw chunks. When the KB was ingested with auto_chunk (long docs split into child chunks), the default behaviour returns whichever chunk matched best. With include_parent the server merges every matched chunk back to its parent, so you receive the complete document. Use this when you need the full context, not just the matching snippet.

response_mode.description: Default compact bounds snippets and omits full content/metadata while preserving every hit and score. Use full for original rows, including full parents with include_parent. Compact returns exact refs for kb_read_item or kb_get_item.

query.description: Natural-language query text (full sentences > terse keywords — the query is embedded the same way as items, so phrasing that mirrors how items were written retrieves best).

include_parent.description: When true, merge child chunk hits back to their parent document before returning. Default false (returns raw matched chunk). Set true when you need full document context rather than just the matching snippet.

include_structure.description: When true, return a bounded, source-derived structure_context with the matched section paths and available heading outline. It never changes search ranking or calls an LLM. Use for long structured documents when an Agent may need to navigate.

mode.description: Retrieval mode. Omit or use semantic for the legacy hybrid search; use relation_aware for canonical entity filters first, bounded graph expansion, and restricted canonical fallback.

entity_types.description: Canonical entity types to resolve first (for example meeting, decision, task). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

project.description: Exact canonical project filter. Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

organization.description: Exact canonical organization filter. Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

event_date.description: Exact canonical event date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware; do not combine with event_date_from or event_date_to.

event_date_from.description: Inclusive canonical event date lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

event_date_to.description: Inclusive canonical event date upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

expand_relations.description: Allowlisted uppercase graph edge types to expand (for example HAS_DECISION or FOLLOW_UP_OF).

context.description: Applicability context for conditions filtering. Only items whose conditions[] all evaluate to true for this context are returned. Items with no conditions always pass. Example: {"env": "production", "lang": "zh"}

tools.name: kb_find_similar
tools.description: Find items semantically near an existing item — a 'more like this' over one KB. Give it an item_id and it fetches that item, then searches the same KB with the item's own text, dropping the item itself (and, for a chunked document, its sibling chunks) from the results. Use it to spot near-duplicates that kb_memory_health's exact-match check misses, to cluster related notes, or to decide whether new knowledge already exists before writing it. Scores are cosine similarity in [0, 1]. Treat < 0.4 as probable noise, but calibrate against the active model — high-band models (bge-m3, e5) score even unrelated content 0.6–0.8, so verify content rather than trusting scores. For exact title+content duplicates prefer kb_memory_health; to search by free text rather than an existing item, use kb_search.

kb_id.description: Knowledge base uuid (from kb_list) holding the anchor item.

item_id.description: Anchor item uuid (from kb_search / kb_list_items). Its text becomes the query.

limit.description: Max similar items to return after dropping the anchor (default 5, max 50).

tools.name: kb_answer
tools.description: Build a bounded evidence pack for a question. Defaults to compact citation previews (at most 2,000 characters each) with exact refs and kb_read_item follow-up instructions. Full mode is still subject to response limits. Citations are numbered in descending score order; retrieval_rank preserves the original server order. top_score is the maximum returned citation or verified escalated score (zero without evidence). A cross-KB answer appears first as escalated_answer only after its own no_answer:false check and confidence floor pass. primary_evidence_ref identifies it; local_no_answer preserves the original KB verdict. Missing or negative no-answer checks never establish confidence. The model-dependent confidence_floor is returned; a high similarity alone does not establish answerability. The default citation gate keeps scores within KB_MCP_CITATION_MARGIN (0.15) of the local maximum and above KB_MCP_CITATION_FLOOR (0.4). min_score overrides that gate. Optional graph and source structure add evidence. Relation-aware mode uses structured filters before semantic fallback. Cross-KB hints remain unverified leads. The opt-in KB_MCP_CITATION_RELEVANCE_ENABLED experiment never overrides explicit min_score. Cite the returned ref and citation number; read the source before relying on a clipped preview. Treat < 0.4 as probable noise, but calibrate against the active model — high-band models (bge-m3, e5) score even unrelated content 0.6–0.8, so verify content rather than trusting scores.

response_mode.description: Defaults to compact citation previews with exact kb_read_item references. Full remains subject to the response size limit.

kb_id.description: Knowledge base uuid (from kb_list) to answer from.

query.description: Natural-language question. Full sentences retrieve best.

limit.description: Max primary citations (default 5, max 50). Compact mode carries bounded parent previews.

min_score.description: Drop citations below this cosine score (0-1). Omit to use the default relevance gate (within KB_MCP_CITATION_MARGIN of the top score, above KB_MCP_CITATION_FLOOR ~0.4); pass 0 to see every raw hit with no filtering at all. The opt-in KB_MCP_CITATION_RELEVANCE_ENABLED experiment never changes explicit min_score calls.

include_graph.description: Graph-expand the hits into neighbouring context (default true). Set false to skip the graph add-on.

include_structure.description: When true, include bounded source-derived section paths, exact source ranges when available, and a local heading outline for cited structured documents. It is evidence only: it does not change ranking, confidence, or call an LLM.

include_multi_vector.description: Fuse helper-vector results into the shortlist. Omit to use the server default.

mode.description: Retrieval mode. Omit or use semantic for the legacy hybrid search; use relation_aware for canonical entity filters first, bounded graph expansion, and restricted canonical fallback.

entity_types.description: Canonical entity types to resolve first (for example meeting, decision, task). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

project.description: Exact canonical project filter. Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

organization.description: Exact canonical organization filter. Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

event_date.description: Exact canonical event date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware; do not combine with event_date_from or event_date_to.

event_date_from.description: Inclusive canonical event date lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

event_date_to.description: Inclusive canonical event date upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

expand_relations.description: Allowlisted uppercase graph edge types to expand (for example HAS_DECISION or FOLLOW_UP_OF).

context.description: Applicability context for conditions filtering. Only items whose conditions[] all evaluate to true for this context are returned. Items with no conditions always pass.

tools.name: kb_search_all
tools.description: Default compact output contains bounded previews and exact references; use response_mode=full for the full rows described below. Cross-KB search. The default is semantic search; set mode=relation_aware with entity/date/project filters when the question asks for canonical events or lineage. Use this when you don't know which KB holds the answer — embedding is computed once and the same RRF ranker fans out across every KB the caller can see (or the explicit kb_ids shortlist). Set `include_brain:true` to union the caller's four managed memory KBs into an explicit shortlist. With no shortlist, all visible KBs already include existing brain buckets; the flag only adds existing buckets and never creates storage on a read. Prefer `kb_recall` for real memory work because it adds confidence floors, staleness warnings, importance, and recency ranking. Each hit carries its `item.knowledge_base_id`; the `knowledge_bases` map in the response gives the KB name/kbid/visibility for each hit so you can render origin without extra round-trips. Prefer the cheaper `kb_search` when the target KB is already known. Scores are cosine similarity in [0, 1]. Treat < 0.4 as probable noise, but calibrate against the active model — high-band models (bge-m3, e5) score even unrelated content 0.6–0.8, so verify content rather than trusting scores.

response_mode.description: Default compact bounds snippets and omits full content/metadata while preserving every hit, score and available KB name. Use full for original rows and knowledge_bases map. Read exact refs with kb_read_item or kb_get_item.

query.description: Natural-language query text. Same embedding pipeline as kb_search.

kb_ids.description: Optional shortlist of KB uuids to restrict the search. Omit to search every KB visible to the caller's tenant. Empty array is rejected.

include_brain.description: When true, find existing managed Brain KBs and add their ids to an explicit kb_ids shortlist (deduplicated). Missing buckets are treated as empty; this read never creates a KB. Default false.

kbcid.description: Optional category filter (kbcid) applied uniformly across selected KBs.

limit.description: Max results (default 10, max 50). Across all KBs combined.

include_structure.description: When true, return bounded source-derived structure_context for the final results. It never changes ranking or calls an LLM.

mode.description: Retrieval mode. Omit or use semantic for the legacy hybrid search; use relation_aware for canonical entity filters first, bounded graph expansion, and restricted canonical fallback.

entity_types.description: Canonical entity types to resolve first (for example meeting, decision, task). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

project.description: Exact canonical project filter. Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

organization.description: Exact canonical organization filter. Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

event_date.description: Exact canonical event date (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware; do not combine with event_date_from or event_date_to.

event_date_from.description: Inclusive canonical event date lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

event_date_to.description: Inclusive canonical event date upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Only applies to mode=relation_aware.

expand_relations.description: Allowlisted uppercase graph edge types to expand (for example HAS_DECISION or FOLLOW_UP_OF).

context.description: Applicability context for conditions filtering. Only items whose conditions[] all evaluate to true for this context are returned. Items with no conditions always pass.

tools.name: kb_begin_structure_navigation
tools.description: Begin a Search-bound deterministic Structure Navigation session. First call kb_search, kb_answer, or kb_search_all and use its search_event_id plus a returned item_id. The KB-API validates tenant, citation membership, and question hash. In paired_evaluation mode, submit the frozen Search-only arm before any navigation action. This tool never calls an LLM Provider.

tools.name: kb_complete_structure_navigation
tools.description: Complete a deterministic Structure Navigation session with the Agent's final answer and exact evidence. Every evidence string must be a substring of the original Search result or a successful navigation trace. Use answer_status=insufficient_evidence when structure is unavailable, hashes/citations fail, or budget is exhausted; the KB-API never falls back to an internal LLM.

tools.name: kb_feedback
tools.description: Close the retrieval feedback loop: rate whether a prior kb_answer / kb_search / kb_search_all actually gave you what the user needed. Pass the `search_event_id` that call returned, plus helpful=true (the context contained the answer) or helpful=false (it did not — wrong, missing, or low-confidence). This is the ONLY signal that turns the Answer-accuracy dashboard from a proxy (top-1 score) into ground truth, so retrieval can be tuned against real outcomes. Only rate when you can judge the result; skip it otherwise. `ok:false` means the id was unknown or not yours.

search_event_id.description: The id returned by the kb_answer / kb_search / kb_search_all call you are rating.

helpful.description: true if the retrieved context contained what the user needed; false if it did not.

reason.description: Optional short explanation of why the result helped or failed.

correct_item_id.description: Optional known-correct item id. Builds a shadow retrieval-profile candidate without changing the item.

tools.name: kb_retrieve
tools.description: Opt-in bounded adaptive retrieval for one knowledge base. It analyzes the query, runs up to three distinct strategies, preserves KB/category/project/date/context constraints on every attempt, and abstains when the canonical evidence gate remains insufficient. The existing Hybrid path remains the default for kb_search/kb_answer. Use strategy=bm25 explicitly for rare technical terms, filenames/paths, error codes, migration names, multiple keyword anchors, or CJK lexical lookups; use depth=fast when BM25-only behavior is required. True pg_search BM25 is never always-on, is never substituted with FTS, and its score is ranking evidence rather than answer confidence. If pg_search is unavailable, inspect the attempt's strategy_available=false and unavailable_reason=bm25_unavailable fields. Inspect attempts, evidence_status, failure_reason, rescued_by, and each result's found_by provenance before answering. The response includes a search_event_id; after judging an explicit BM25 result, use kb_feedback to record useful/not_useful, or omit it when unknown.

kb_id.description: Knowledge base UUID. This scope is retained for every attempt.

strategy.description: Initial strategy. Use bm25 only when lexical intent justifies it; pair with depth=fast for a pure specialist call. auto selects from deterministic query analysis. Other explicit strategies may use bounded complementary fallbacks unless depth=fast.

reason_selected.description: Required for explicit Agent choices when known; bounded reason for selecting the initial strategy.

previous_strategy.description: Optional preceding strategy for content-free selection telemetry; it does not alter retrieval.

previous_evidence_status.description: Optional preceding evidence-gate status for content-free selection telemetry.

depth.description: fast runs one attempt; adaptive/deep allow at most three distinct attempts. Default adaptive.

journey_id.description: Optional caller-owned correlation id. It is returned but not copied into content telemetry.

context.description: Applicability/profile context retained unchanged across every attempt.

tools.name: kb_memory_health
tools.description: Audit the quality of everything the caller can see, grouped by issue. Read-only; never writes. Use this to self-check your long-term memory: it surfaces items with `missing_structured_metadata` (no memory_type / project / confidence / source_kind), `stale_items` (past expires_at or older than the staleness hint), `low_confidence_items` (confidence unverified/inferred/low or score < 0.6), `duplicate_candidates` (exact title+content matches — feed these to kb_merge), and `contradiction_candidates` (items joined by an explicit CONTRADICTS relation). `summary` gives counts; each group lists up to `limit` example items. `summary.confidence_root_causes` further separates potential metadata drift, inferred-by-design, genuine uncertainty, malformed labels, and conflicts; it is diagnostic only and never authorizes promotion. `summary.actionable_low_confidence_items` (V2) is the subset of low_confidence_items that still needs work once trusted lifecycle/applicability is accounted for: a low-confidence item bound to a server-issued applicability review (never a plain metadata claim, which is not trusted on its own) as historical/superseded is excluded here even though it stays in the raw low_confidence_items count. See `v2` for the full Evidence x Temporal Role x Applicability x Freshness -> Disposition breakdown. This tool defaults to detail:'summary' — compact refs (id/kb/title/reasons) per example, bounded output even at limit=100. Pass detail:'full' only when you actually need content previews + metadata per example (a full limit=100 report can exceed 100k tokens). Also defaults to scope:'brain' — only kb-mcp's own managed brain KBs are checked, since missing_structured_metadata/low_confidence key off memory_type/project/confidence/source_kind, fields that only brain memories are expected to carry (2026-07-28 E2E report: an unscoped sweep flagged 68% of everything visible, mostly Tool Registry/project-doc items, not memory quality issues). Pass scope:'all' for a KB-wide sweep instead. A good periodic hygiene loop: kb_memory_health → kb_merge the duplicate groups → kb_update_memory the low-confidence/missing-metadata items → kb_forget the truly stale ones.

limit.description: Max example items per issue group (default 20, max 100). Does not cap the summary counts.

stale_days.description: Age threshold in days for the staleness_hint check (default 90). Items whose staleness_hint_days is set and whose updated_at is older than this count as stale.

detail.description: Example-item verbosity. Default 'summary' (compact refs: id, kb, title, reasons). 'full' adds content_preview + complete metadata per example — large; use only when needed.

scope.description: Which KBs to check. Default 'brain' (kb-mcp's own agent-brain-* KBs only). 'all' sweeps every visible KB, same as the raw HTTP endpoint's default.

tools.name: kb_confidence_reconciliation_report
tools.description: Read-only confidence root-cause audit for a master-scoped operator. Classifies low-confidence memories into potential metadata drift, inferred-by-design, genuinely unverified, missing/malformed labels, and conflicting evidence. It never promotes or edits knowledge. Labels, LLM output and source fingerprints are discovery signals only, not verification authority. Defaults to scope:'brain', detail:'summary'.

scope.description: Default 'brain'; use 'all' for every visible KB.

limit.description: Maximum examples; summary totals are not capped.

detail.description: Default 'summary'; full includes metadata and source fingerprint.

tools.name: kb_confidence_evidence
tools.description: Issue source-bound Agent confirmation as an authenticated master Agent. Read the current source fingerprint first. This retains machine provenance and can support confirmed confidence, never independent verified confidence. The server validates identity and scope; unsupported verifier claims are rejected.

tools.name: kb_confidence_preview
tools.description: Build a deterministic master-scoped confidence repair plan from server-issued evidence IDs. Does not modify knowledge. Inspect actions, dry-run, then apply using the same authenticated Agent. Inference and contradiction gates remain enforced.

tools.name: kb_confidence_apply
tools.description: Dry-run or apply a deterministic confidence plan as its creating master Agent. Revalidates current evidence, item fingerprints, permissions and expiry. confirm:true acknowledges the exact selected actions; no human login is required. Repeating the same completed selection is idempotent.

tools.name: kb_memory_applicability_review
tools.description: Record a master Agent's source-bound applicability judgment for an active canonical memory. Requires the current source fingerprint and visible canonical evidence references in KB-UUID:item-UUID form. Records real Agent provenance. Changes Health interpretation without changing retrieval lifecycle or deleting content.

tools.name: kb_memory_collaboration
tools.description: Create, resolve, change members or revoke a collaboration. An authenticated Agent manages only spaces it created in its own profile, with active same-profile members and bounded lifetime (default 24h, maximum 7d). Existing owner/other-Agent spaces cannot be taken over. Create/resolve need collaboration_key; members/revoke need collaboration_id; create/members need agent_keys.

tools.name: kb_archive
tools.description: Preview one reversible memory archive or restore. This tool never mutates memory: it returns a short-lived lifecycle plan. Review its actions, then pass the plan_id and explicit action_ids to kb_bulk_manage apply mode. Archived memories are excluded from normal retrieval by default.

memory_id.description: Opaque <kb_id>:<item_id> memory_id returned by kb_remember or kb_recall.

action.description: Lifecycle transition to preview. Default archive; restore reactivates an archived memory.

tools.name: kb_bulk_manage
tools.description: Preview or apply controlled memory lifecycle operations. Preview mode accepts up to 20 explicit memory operations and never mutates. Apply mode requires the short-lived plan_id plus an explicit, non-empty action_ids selection; dry_run defaults to true. Set dry_run=false only after reviewing both the preview and dry-run result. This full-admin tool supports update, archive, restore, merge, delete, and automatic private-to-user promotion.

memory_id.description: Opaque <kb_id>:<item_id> memory_id returned by kb_remember or kb_recall.

operations.description: Preview mode only: explicit update/archive/restore/merge/delete/promote operations. Authorized callers may promote automatically after preview; apply revalidates scope and source provenance.

plan_id.description: Apply mode only: plan_id returned by a lifecycle preview.

action_ids.description: Apply mode only: explicit action ids selected from the reviewed plan. Never inferred or omitted.

dry_run.description: Apply mode defaults to dry-run. Set false only after reviewing the dry-run result.

tools.name: kb_optimize_analyze
tools.description: Analyze one visible knowledge base and create a 30-minute server-authored optimization plan. Read the returned actions before applying. Deterministic actions may normalize outer whitespace or add labels fully resolved by existing rules; exact and semantic near-duplicates, uncertain labels, and missing embeddings are review-only. This tool never deletes knowledge.

semantic_threshold.description: Model-dependent cosine threshold for bounded review-only near-duplicate candidates (default 0.95)

tools.name: kb_optimize_apply
tools.description: Validate or apply deterministic actions from kb_optimize_analyze. Defaults to dry_run=true. Use the plan_id and optionally choose up to 20 apply-mode action_ids. The server rejects expired, already-used, foreign, review-only, or stale plans atomically. It never applies duplicate deletion.

kb_id.description: Knowledge base uuid used for analysis

plan_id.description: Short-lived plan id returned by kb_optimize_analyze

action_ids.description: Apply only these apply-mode actions; omit to select every applicable action (max 20)

dry_run.description: Default true. Set false only after reviewing the plan and dry-run result.

tools.name: kb_tool_search
tools.description: Search approved agent tool definitions stored as normal KB items. Tool Registry v1 is read-only: this tool discovers contracts; it never executes code. A matching item must use kbcid='agent.tool' and metadata.kind='tool'. The response returns tool_id values for kb_tool_get.

query.description: Natural-language tool need, e.g. 'check production health' or 'transform csv to json'.

kb_ids.description: Optional KB shortlist. Omit to search every visible KB for kbcid='agent.tool'.

runtime.description: Optional runtime filter applied after retrieval.

safety_level.description: Optional safety filter applied after retrieval.

limit.description: Max tools to return after filtering (default 10, max 20).

tools.name: kb_tool_get
tools.description: Fetch one full Tool Registry v1 definition by tool_id from kb_tool_search. This is read-only and does not execute code. It validates that the backing item still has metadata.kind='tool'.

tool_id.description: Opaque tool id returned by kb_tool_search, formatted '<kb_uuid>:<item_uuid>'.

tools.name: kb_tool_sandbox_status
tools.description: Report whether THIS KB-MCP host can actually execute Tool Registry node/shell tools right now, without needing to register a throwaway tool first just to find out. Surfaces the same sandbox_compatibility verdict kb_tool_test computes per-tool (Node version, whether the permission model's network-deny is enforced, KB_TOOL_ALLOW_UNENFORCED_NET, the read-only shell binary allowlist) as a standalone, always-available diagnostic. Added 2026-07-28: a Node-version-locked host reporting sandbox_compatibility:false per-tool was correct but only discoverable after registering something.

tools.name: kb_tool_register
tools.description: Create one Tool Registry definition as a normal KB item using kbcid='agent.tool' and metadata.kind='tool'. This stores contracts, artifacts, and harness metadata only; it does not execute code.

kb_id.description: Target knowledge base uuid for the tool definition.

description.description: What the tool does and when an agent should use it.

runtime.description: Runtime the artifact is meant for.

content.description: Human-readable runbook/body for the tool definition.

source.description: Optional provenance tag or source path.

requires_approval.description: Override approval requirement. Defaults true for remote/destructive writes.

allowed_env.description: Env var allowlist for future sandbox execution.

verified_at.description: ISO timestamp of last successful harness verification.

artifacts.description: Versioned artifact metadata. Examples: { kind:'inline', language:'node', content:'...', sha256:'...' } or { kind:'git', ref:'repo/path#commit', sha256:'...' }.

harness.description: Harness metadata such as { sample_input, expected_output_schema, expected_text }. kb_tool_test validates shape only.

metadata.description: Additional metadata to merge after required Tool Registry fields.

update_item_id.description: Existing canonical Tool Registry item id to update instead of creating a duplicate.

tools.name: kb_tool_test
tools.description: Validate one Tool Registry definition's contract, artifact metadata, and harness metadata without executing code. This is a metadata/harness gate for future sandbox execution.

tool_id.description: Opaque tool id returned by kb_tool_search or kb_tool_register.

tools.name: kb_tool_set_trust
tools.description: Promote or demote a Tool Registry definition's trust_status (draft/trusted/deprecated). This is the ONLY supported way to change trust_status: the server locks trust_status and trust_history against direct writes via kb_update_item for kind='tool' items (2026-07-28 E2E follow-up -- a plain metadata PATCH used to silently self-promote a draft tool with zero audit trail). Promoting to 'trusted' requires a currently-passing kb_tool_test result for THIS exact artifact -- run kb_tool_test first. Editing the artifact afterwards automatically reverts trust_status to 'draft'. Every change is appended to metadata.trust_history with the reason, approver, timestamp, and artifact fingerprint.

tool_id.description: Opaque tool id returned by kb_tool_search or kb_tool_register.

approved_by.description: Who/what is making this change (name, role, or agent id) -- recorded in metadata.trust_history.

reason.description: Why this change is being made -- recorded in metadata.trust_history.

tools.name: kb_tool_run
tools.description: Execute one approved Tool Registry definition in the constrained sandbox. Trusted read-only tools can run directly unless policy marks their safety level as approval-required. Non-read-only or approval-required tools must match an exact-version autonomous pre-approval policy; when policy requires a dry run, preview first and pass its one-use dry_run_receipt on the same session with unchanged input within five minutes. writes_local Node tools can execute in an isolated output dir with manifest, verification, and cleanup metadata. writes_remote/destructive tools stay dry-run only. HTTP tools must use same-origin GET artifacts. Shell/node tools run in a bounded worker process with timeout, output caps, env allowlist, and isolated temp files. Python/sql artifacts remain discovery-only and are rejected.

tool_id.description: Opaque tool id returned by kb_tool_search or kb_tool_register.

input.description: Optional tool input. Sandbox v1 does not interpolate input into URLs; this is returned for harness traceability.

dry_run.description: When true, validate and return the resolved action without executing it. Required previews return a session-bound one-use receipt.

dry_run_receipt.description: Receipt from a successful dry run in this session. Required when the matching preapproval requires a dry run; consumed before execution and never reusable.

tools.name: kb_reuse_context
tools.description: Mandatory engineering reuse gate. Decomposes a meaningful task into independent capability units, searches visible Skill Registry, Tool Registry, Brain layers, project KBs and shared KBs through the tenant-scoped KB-API search surface, then returns a structured Reuse Pack. Use the pack to Reuse verified protocols, Adapt project experience, Avoid known pitfalls, and Research only explicit gaps. A meaningful task is fail-closed when retrieval is unavailable or partial; a genuine no-prior-art result permits fresh research. Engineering implementation also requires preflight_evidence and current-source validation. Read-only routing never authorizes writes. Tiny UI/copy edits are exempt.

task.description: The engineering task or project request.

changes_engineering_artifacts.description: Set true when the runtime will change source or engineering artifacts. This requires retrieval regardless of routing or task wording; false cannot waive a detected engineering task.

preflight_evidence.description: Required before implementation: current source observations, dependency paths, reviewed KB evidence, risks and planned verification. Host validation is required for source-read and execution claims.

mode.description: Reuse mode. Defaults to mandatory. `off` is reported as a blocked bypass for meaningful work.

project.description: Current project or repository label for applicability scoring.

context.description: Bounded environment/context facts used for applicability and compatibility review.

max_matches_per_capability.description: Maximum hits per capability/layer query; default 6.

tools.name: kb_engineering_reflect
tools.description: Validate regression and reflection evidence for a session-owned engineering preflight, send retrieval feedback, and read back lessons written through existing Brain lifecycle tools. Missing checks, feedback or required lesson writes block completion. Source-read and test-execution claims still require independent host validation; this tool never edits source or writes memory.

tools.name: kb_reuse_feedback
tools.description: Record whether a Reuse Pack was useful and which retrieved items were actually selected. This uses the existing tenant-scoped search-event feedback and selection infrastructure; it never stores the task text or knowledge content.

search_event_ids.description: Search event ids from Reuse Pack telemetry.

useful.description: Whether the retrieved reuse context helped the implementation.

implementation_reused.description: Whether the final implementation reused or adapted a retrieved item.

external_research_needed.description: Whether the agent had to research a reported gap.

tools.name: kb_reuse_lesson_propose
tools.description: Proposal-only verified lesson capture for cross-project engineering reuse. Fetches only the referenced knowledge items, checks source provenance, applicability, independent test/replay evidence, and conflict review, then returns an owner-reviewable lesson/Skill packet. This tool never writes memory, Skill Registry items, relations, or source content; call kb_remember_preview and the reviewed write tools only after explicit owner approval.

task_fingerprint.description: Lowercase SHA-256 fingerprint of the bounded task context.

tools.name: kb_rsi_status
tools.description: Read-only RSI control-plane status for the caller's tenant: promotion lock, policy fingerprint, and bounded failure/candidate/experiment/rollout counts. It never reads raw query text or changes serving behavior.

tools.name: kb_rsi_failures
tools.description: List content-free RSI failure observations visible to the caller. Use this to see failure type/state/reason codes and bounded fingerprints; raw query and item content are intentionally excluded.

tools.name: kb_rsi_candidates
tools.description: List content-free RSI candidates visible to the caller. Shows immutable target fingerprints, authority, state, and bounded provenance without exposing knowledge-item titles or content.

tools.name: kb_rsi_candidate_history
tools.description: Read the append-only decisions, shadow/rolling experiments, and rollout history for one visible RSI candidate. Read-only and content-free.

tools.name: kb_rsi_candidate_compare
tools.description: Compare the two newest immutable RSI experiments for one visible candidate, including bounded latency/error deltas and the newest rollout. Read-only; no candidate promotion or pause action is available here.

tools.name: kb_rsi_control_status
tools.description: Read the master-only RSI control dashboard: global promotion lock, 17-gate evidence, worker lease, consent summaries, shared optimizer budget, rollout counts, and bounded audit decisions. It never returns item titles/content and never changes state.

tools.name: kb_rsi_propose
tools.description: Master-scope owner action: move a diagnosed RSI candidate into proposed review. The API enforces tenant scope, monotonic state, consent, and append-only audit.

tools.name: kb_rsi_experiment
tools.description: Master-scope owner action: create a fingerprint-bound, planned RSI sandbox experiment. It records intent only; no replay, serving change, or knowledge mutation runs.

tools.name: kb_rsi_pause
tools.description: Master-scope RSI pause. Candidate rollout pauses are master-authorized; a global promotion-lock pause is root-only and always audited.

candidate_id.description: Optional candidate; omit for root-only global pause/resume

tools.name: kb_rsi_resume
tools.description: Master-scope RSI resume. Candidate rollout resume is master-authorized; only root may resume the globally paused lock back to locked (never directly to unlocked).

candidate_id.description: Optional candidate; omit for root-only global pause/resume

tools.name: kb_rsi_promote
tools.description: Master-scope RSI promotion request. The API remains fail-closed until current 17/17 fingerprints, canary evidence, and a real serving router exist; it cannot activate a profile.

tools.name: kb_rsi_rollback
tools.description: Master-scope RSI rollback. It marks registry/rollout evidence rolled_back and never edits knowledge items, vectors, relations, or serving defaults.

tools.name: kb_rsi_policy
tools.description: Root-only RSI policy append. The server validates the controlled-rsi-v1 shape and computes the SHA-256 hash; this never unlocks the promotion lock.

tools.name: kb_read_item
tools.description: Read exact knowledge by bare item UUID or kb_uuid:item_uuid, including supported historical aliases. Returns canonical reference and reader_path. Content is paginated by Unicode characters: continue with reference, version and next_offset until next_offset is null. Never use semantic search to resolve an identifier.

tools.name: kb_list_items
tools.description: Default compact output contains bounded previews and exact references; use response_mode=full for the full rows described below. List items in a KB (paginated). Returns id, title, content_preview, source, image_url, metadata. Use kb_get_item to fetch the full content of a single item. Supports three optional server-side filters that mirror the same parameter names accepted by kb_search_all where applicable — prefer these over fetching everything and filtering client-side: `search` (title/content keyword, FTS for ASCII queries and pg_trgm for CJK / non-ASCII), `kbcid` (server-indexed category column), and `tag` (single tag inside `metadata.tags` JSONB array). All three combine with AND.

response_mode.description: Default compact omits bulky metadata, bounds previews and preserves every reference, applicability information and pagination. Full preserves original list rows. Content remains incomplete; read exact references with kb_read_item. If references cannot fit, reduce limit and retry the same offset.

search.description: Title/content keyword filter. ASCII queries use Postgres FTS (English stemming + ts_rank weighting, title=A content=B); non-ASCII queries (CJK etc.) fall back to pg_trgm ILIKE so retrieval stays language-agnostic. Not the same as semantic search — use kb_search / kb_search_all for vector similarity.

kbcid.description: Filter by server-indexed category id (the column, not metadata). Same string you'd pass to kb_search_all's `kbcid`. Examples: 'agrun.runtime', 'infra.readurl'.

entity_type.description: Filter by entity_type (exact match, case-sensitive). Set at write time via kb_add_item's entity_type field. Examples: 'fact', 'bug', 'api_endpoint'.

tag.description: Filter by a single tag inside `metadata.tags` (JSONB array containment, case-sensitive exact match). Items written with `metadata: { tags: ['x', 'y'] }` match `tag: 'x'` or `tag: 'y'` but not `tag: 'X'`.

metadata_kind.description: Filter by exact `metadata.kind`. Useful for structured item conventions such as life ledger records (`life_ledger_record`).

metadata_date_from.description: Inclusive lower bound for `metadata.date` in YYYY-MM-DD format.

metadata_date_to.description: Inclusive upper bound for `metadata.date` in YYYY-MM-DD format.

context.description: Applicability context for conditions filtering. Items whose conditions[] do not all evaluate to true for this context are excluded. Items with no conditions always pass. With context, `total` is the context-filtered count and limit/offset page the FILTERED sequence; `total_before_context_filter` carries the raw count. (For KBs past an internal size cap the response degrades to page-level filtering and says so in `context_filter_note`.)

tools.name: kb_get_item
tools.description: Fetch a single knowledge item by id (full content). Use this after kb_list_items when you need the complete content field rather than the preview.

tools.name: kb_open_section
tools.description: Open one bounded, exact Markdown section from a V17 Document IR item. First use kb_search/kb_answer with include_structure:true to obtain a source-owned outline node_id, then pass that node_id here. The server resolves a retrieved child id to its canonical parent, validates the stored Document IR against the canonical source bytes, and returns only the requested section page. This is deterministic/local navigation — it does not search, infer, plan, or call an LLM Provider. Legacy or stale structure returns STRUCTURE_UNAVAILABLE rather than guessed text.

item_id.description: Parent or retrieved child uuid (from a search result or structure_context)

offset.description: Zero-based offset within this one section; use next_offset to continue

max_chars.description: Maximum section characters to return (default 6000, max 12000)

navigation_session_id.description: Required Search-bound navigation session id from kb_begin_structure_navigation

tools.name: kb_list_pdf_outline
tools.description: List compact native PDF bookmarks for a source that the supplied retrieved item actually cites. First use kb_get_item_provenance to obtain document_id, then call this only for a cited selectable PDF. The server returns only source-bound native outline nodes; it does not search, infer a document hierarchy, plan navigation, or call an LLM Provider. If the PDF has no exact trusted native outline, it returns PDF_STRUCTURE_UNAVAILABLE instead of guessed headings.

item_id.description: Retrieved/imported item uuid that cites the source document

document_id.description: Cited PDF document uuid from kb_get_item_provenance

navigation_session_id.description: Required Search-bound navigation session id from kb_begin_structure_navigation

tools.name: kb_open_pdf_outline_node
tools.description: Open one bounded, exact source PAGE SLICE at a node from kb_list_pdf_outline. This intentionally does not claim a PDF section end because bookmark order may not match physical reading order. The source bytes, page text proof, node manifest, and citation relation are revalidated server-side. This is deterministic/local navigation and never calls an LLM Provider.

item_id.description: Retrieved/imported item uuid that cites the source document

document_id.description: Cited PDF document uuid from kb_get_item_provenance

offset.description: Zero-based offset after the node anchor on its one source page

navigation_session_id.description: Required Search-bound navigation session id from kb_begin_structure_navigation

tools.name: kb_list_pdf_tagged_structure
tools.description: List exact native PDF table-row and internal-reference candidates for a source that the supplied retrieved item actually cites. First use kb_get_item_provenance to obtain document_id, then call this only for a cited selectable PDF. The server returns only hash-bound source candidates; it does not search, infer table cells, follow references, plan navigation, or call an LLM Provider. If native tags cannot bind exactly to stored source text, it returns PDF_STRUCTURE_UNAVAILABLE instead of a guessed structure.

item_id.description: Retrieved/imported item uuid that cites the source document

document_id.description: Cited PDF document uuid from kb_get_item_provenance

navigation_session_id.description: Required Search-bound navigation session id from kb_begin_structure_navigation

tools.name: kb_open_pdf_tagged_candidate
tools.description: Open one exact source table row or internal-reference text range from kb_list_pdf_tagged_structure. The source bytes, candidate manifest, stored page proof, and citation relation are revalidated server-side. For a reference, target page/top is returned only as a locator: it is never auto-followed. This is deterministic/local navigation and never calls OCR or an LLM Provider.

item_id.description: Retrieved/imported item uuid that cites the source document

document_id.description: Cited PDF document uuid from kb_get_item_provenance

navigation_session_id.description: Required Search-bound navigation session id from kb_begin_structure_navigation

tools.name: kb_get_item_provenance
tools.description: List the SOURCE PROVENANCE (proof-of-origin) of an imported knowledge item: which document and page each fact came from, the bbox region on the page, and the size + MIME of the stored proof image for that page. This is the cheap, no-bytes call — use it to show an end user WHERE the data came from, and to decide (via image_byte_size) whether to pull the actual page image with kb_get_source_image. Returns an empty list for items with no source pages (e.g. manually typed items or pre-provenance imports).

item_id.description: Item uuid (from kb_list_items, kb_search, or kb_get_item)

tools.name: kb_get_source_image
tools.description: Fetch the stored PROOF IMAGE of one source page as evidence — the visual proof of where an imported item's knowledge came from. Returns bounded metadata with the authenticated page URL, byte size and MIME; JSON never contains Base64 image data. Includes one MCP image block for raster types (jpeg/png/gif/webp) only when the entire tool result fits the configured response budget. Oversized or non-raster images return image_block_included=false with an omission reason and next_action to view the original through the authenticated URL. Get document_id + page_no from kb_get_item_provenance.

tools.name: kb_update_item
tools.description: Partially update a knowledge item (PATCH). Only include fields you want to change. If title or content is present, the server re-embeds the item automatically. Three-state contract: omit a field = keep unchanged; pass null = clear (kbcid, source, image_url); pass a value = update. metadata is replaced wholesale — send the full object you want stored. For Tool Registry items (metadata.kind='tool') the server always keeps its own stored trust_status/trust_history regardless of what you submit here — use kb_tool_set_trust to change trust_status.

kbcid.description: Server-indexed category id. Three-state: omit = keep, null = clear, value = set. Pattern: 1-64 chars, lowercase a-z 0-9 . _ -. Same field filtered by kb_search_all.

share_level.description: New explicit item tier. Omit to keep the current tier.

source.description: Provenance tag. Pass null to clear.

image_url.description: HTTPS URL or data:image/...;base64,… inline URI. Pass null to clear.

metadata.description: Replacement metadata object (not merged — send full desired object). For an already-versioned canonical item, read it with kb_get_item first and retain every required canonical field when replacing metadata. Omitting metadata leaves it unchanged. Legacy unversioned rows retain their existing PATCH behavior. For a reserved canonical entity_type, metadata is required: entity_schema_version, canonical_key, status, source_document_id. entity_schema_version must be 1; canonical_key is a stable identifier without spaces; source_document_id identifies the supporting source and is separate from the item's source field. status must be one of draft, planned, confirmed, completed, cancelled, unknown. Additional required fields — meeting: event_date, timezone, participants, project, organization; event: event_date, timezone, participants; task: ticket; commit: commit_sha; test_result: test_key, outcome. event_date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD calendar date; timezone uses an IANA-style name; participants is an array of strings (an empty array is accepted). ticket and test_key must not contain spaces; commit_sha is a 7–64 digit hexadecimal Git object id. outcome must be one of passed, failed, skipped, blocked, unknown. Complete event example (replace illustrative values with source-backed values): {"entity_schema_version":1,"canonical_key":"example:record","status":"confirmed","source_document_id":"example-source-document","event_date":"2026-09-27","timezone":"Asia/Singapore","participants":[]}. Other metadata keys remain supported. For non-canonical types, metadata is optional free-form JSON. Never fabricate a source, date, participant or identity.

tools.name: kb_delete_item
tools.description: Permanently delete a knowledge item. This is a hard delete — the item and its embedding are removed immediately and cannot be recovered. Confirm the item id with kb_list_items or kb_get_item before calling.

tools.name: kb_life_ledger_add
tools.description: Create or update one Personal Life Ledger record using a stable metadata schema for daily expenses, meals, calorie estimates, and life events. The tool first scans existing `kbcid='life.ledger'` records on the same date for likely duplicates. If a likely duplicate exists, it returns duplicate_candidates and does not create a new item unless `force_create` is true or `update_item_id` is supplied.

kb_id.description: Target knowledge base uuid (from kb_list). Use a personal/private KB.

date.description: Local ledger date in YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-05-28.

time.description: Optional local time, HH:mm or HH:mm:ss.

timezone.description: IANA timezone or offset label, e.g. Asia/Kuala_Lumpur.

record_type.description: Record type, e.g. expense, meal, life_event, health, travel, work.

category.description: Human category, e.g. grooming, food, transport.

merchant.description: Merchant or counterparty, e.g. Kopitiam, barber shop.

amount.description: Expense amount. Omit for non-expense or unknown amount.

currency.description: Currency code, e.g. SGD, MYR, USD.

calories_kcal.description: Estimated calories in kcal for meals/food.

calorie_confidence.description: Calorie confidence, e.g. high, medium, low, estimated.

source_type.description: Source kind, e.g. message, screenshot, receipt, manual.

source_reference.description: Stable source id/path/hash/message id when available.

confidence.description: Overall extraction confidence, e.g. high, medium, low, inferred.

notes.description: Extra details from the user message, OCR, receipt, or assistant inference.

tags.description: Export/search tags. life-ledger/type/category are added automatically.

title.description: Optional explicit title. If omitted, a stable title is generated.

activity.description: Optional activity label, e.g. haircut, lunch, gym.

force_create.description: Create even when duplicate candidates are found. Default false.

update_item_id.description: Patch this existing item instead of creating a new one.

duplicate_limit.description: Max duplicate candidates to return. Default 5.

tools.name: kb_life_ledger_query
tools.description: Query Personal Life Ledger records by inclusive date range. Returns matching records, daily/weekly/monthly-ready aggregates, and stable export rows/columns for CSV or Google Sheets. This is a structured ledger scan, not semantic search.

max_scan_items.description: Safety cap for paginated scan. Default 1000.

tools.name: kb_life_ledger_report
tools.description: Return a daily/weekly report helper payload for Personal Life Ledger records: expense summary, calorie summary, notable events, uncertain records, and suggested next actions. Use this for prompts like '今天总结' after choosing the date range.

max_scan_items.description: Safety cap for paginated scan. Default 1000.

tools.name: kb_brain_remember
tools.description: Default Agent Brain write. Save one durable memory using deterministic type/metadata defaults, semantic duplicate checks, contradiction safeguards, user-only sharing, embedding, and retry-safe storage. Ambiguous duplicates or contradictions return status:'needs_review' without writing.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key reused only for an exact retry.

tools.name: kb_brain_recall
tools.description: Default Agent Brain read. Retrieve relevant long-term memories through the existing ranked, deduplicated, tenant-scoped pipeline. Contract evidence-v2: retrieval_confidence describes relevance; answerable is true only when enabled belief resolution establishes sufficient evidence. Otherwise verify sources; no serving is enabled by this tool.

project.description: Optional project scope for legacy recall and belief resolution.

environment.description: Optional environment scope for belief resolution.

resolve_belief.description: Request belief resolution when the server serving flag is enabled.

collapse_semantic_duplicates.description: Collapse validated semantic-overlap members to one visible representative when the server rollout flag permits it; preserves source memories and provenance.

tools.name: kb_brain_update
tools.description: Default Agent Brain update. Target by memory_id or semantic query. Semantic targeting fails closed unless exactly one confident candidate exists within the top-hit 0.10 similarity band. Ambiguity returns needs_review normally.

tools.name: kb_brain_forget
tools.description: Default safe forget. Reversibly archive one memory through the backend lifecycle authority. This facade never performs an irreversible hard delete.

tools.name: kb_brain_context
tools.description: Default one-call context assembly. Reuse the existing Agent Profile, long-term/recent memory, Skill Router, Role Contract, and engineering Reuse Pack orchestration before answering a message. The optional mode and budget hints are server-resolved; meaningful engineering work always retains the mandatory Reuse Pack gate.

changes_engineering_artifacts.description: Set true for source or engineering artifact changes. This promotes engineering mode and requires reuse even when the message looks read-only.

resolve_belief.description: Request the deterministic current-belief pack; server serving policy may return disabled or unavailable instead of certainty.

mode.description: Server-owned context mode hint. Meaningful engineering work is promoted to engineering so the mandatory Reuse Pack gate cannot be bypassed.

recent_context_projection.description: Optional Recent Context response contract. Defaults to bounded_v2 in every mode; explicit legacy_v1 remains subject to the final response budget.

max_memories.description: Bounded maximum long-term memories; the effective mode may apply a lower safe ceiling.

max_context_chars.description: Optional hard serialized-response character budget. Required safety evidence is never silently truncated.

max_context_tokens_hint.description: Optional soft token target measured by the reported heuristic estimator. It may produce target_exceeded but is not a client-model hard cap; use max_context_chars for a deterministic hard limit.

tools.name: kb_brain_status
tools.description: Compact Agent Brain health summary. Checks owned KB-API liveness/readiness, memory health, recent context, and a real scoped search whose results are discarded. It never calls an external LLM provider.

tools.name: kb_brain_belief_resolve
tools.description: Explicit read-only Agent Brain belief resolution. Search only the caller's existing four Brain buckets, collect tenant-scoped candidates, recheck source visibility/version, and return the deterministic current or historical belief result. Untrusted metadata never promotes evidence; this tool does not change legacy recall or serving behavior and returns insufficient/unavailable when the verifier or evidence is missing.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to interpret a bounded range. Explicit range timestamps must include an offset; bounded range results are chronological changes; weak or conflicting evidence remains insufficient.

tools.name: kb_brain_whoami
tools.description: Read-only Agent identity and Brain capability projection from the authenticated KB-MCP/KB-API context. It reports server-derived scope, workspace/realm, profile and existing four Brain bucket status. It never exposes bearer tokens or API keys and never creates missing buckets.

tools.name: kb_ingest_conversation
tools.description: Extract reviewable memory candidates from a conversation transcript. This is a preview/review flow: it returns pending drafts with kb_remember_preview results and never writes automatically. Approve a candidate by calling kb_remember with its text and metadata.

project.description: Project/domain label to stamp into candidate preview metadata.

source_agent.description: Agent identity to preserve on structured episodic candidates.

tools.name: kb_bootstrap
tools.description: Session bootstrap helper. Call this at the start of a new session using the first user message. Retrieves canonical Current Context plus top-N relevant long-term memories AND (optionally) loads the agent's stored profile (persona, behavior rules, project assignments) in parallel — no second round-trip needed. Returns memory_context with the profile section prepended when agent_id is supplied. Never writes memory; KB-API does not auto-inject anything.

first_user_message.description: The first user message or task brief for the new session.

agent_id.description: Optional agent identifier. When supplied, the agent's stored profile (persona, behavior rules, project assignments) is fetched in parallel and merged into memory_context. Use the same id passed to kb_set_agent_profile.

collaboration_id.description: Optional explicit collaboration scope. Only bounded member notes are included; collaboration is never inferred.

k.description: Max memories to include in the bootstrap context (default 8).

types.description: Restrict to specific memory buckets. Omit to search all four.

tools.name: kb_agent_context
tools.description: One-call agent context assembly for a new task. It loads the optional Agent Profile and relevant memories, routes the user message to a Skill Registry workflow, runs the mandatory engineering Reuse Pack gate for meaningful work, then returns a temporary Role Contract. The role is lower-priority guidance only: it never overrides system, repository, safety, or current user instructions. This tool is read-only and does not auto-inject anything into an agent prompt. A coding orchestrator must not begin implementation when reuse_pack.gate.implementation_allowed is false.

first_user_message.description: The first user message or task brief for the new task.

changes_engineering_artifacts.description: Set true for source or engineering artifact changes. This requires reuse regardless of routing or task wording.

context.description: Optional extra routing context, not a replacement for the user message.
