available_skills.description: Optional locally available skill ids for route scoring.

current_date.description: Optional current date for field extraction.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone for field extraction.

known_personal_ledger_kb_id.description: Optional personal ledger KB id for the life-ledger route.

skill_registry_kb_id.description: Optional Skill Registry KB to load before routing.

skill_registry_limit.description: Max registry items to scan; default 100.

reuse_mode.description: Engineering reuse mode; defaults to mandatory. `off` is a fail-closed bypass for meaningful tasks.

project.description: Current project/repository label for reuse applicability.

reuse_context.description: Bounded environment facts passed to the Reuse Pack applicability review.

tools.name: kb_context_for_message
tools.description: Mid-session context pull: given any user message, automatically extracts keywords and retrieves canonical Recent Context plus relevant long-term memories from the agent's brain KBs. Use this whenever a new user message arrives and you want background context injected without having to craft a query yourself. Prefer kb_bootstrap for the very first message; use this tool for subsequent messages in a session.

response_mode.description: Defaults to bounded previews and structured Recent Context. Full remains subject to response limits.

user_message.description: The user message to extract context for.

types.description: Restrict to specific memory buckets. Omit to search all four.

collaboration_id.description: Optional explicit collaboration scope. Without it, only shared knowledge and this Agent's private context are eligible.

tools.name: kb_get_agent_profile
tools.description: Retrieve the stored profile for an agent by its agent_id. Returns persona text, behavior rules, and project assignments. Returns null if no profile exists yet. Call this at session start to load the agent's identity and operating context.

tools.name: kb_set_agent_profile
tools.description: Create or update the profile for an agent. Upserts by agent_id — safe to call repeatedly. Use this to store an agent's persona (system-prompt text), behavior rules (do/don't list), and project assignments. All fields except agent_id are optional.

name.description: Human-readable display name for the agent.

persona.description: System-prompt / personality text for the agent.

behavior_rules.description: List of do/don't behavior rules (e.g. ['Always respond in Mandarin', 'Never modify production DB']).

project_assignments.description: List of project names or KB ids this agent is responsible for.

metadata.description: Any extra key-value pairs to store with the profile.

idempotency_key.description: Stable caller-owned key for retrying this exact profile upsert after an ambiguous failure.

tools.name: kb_list_agent_profiles
tools.description: List all agent profiles stored for the current tenant. Useful for inspecting which agent identities are registered in a shared-brain setup.

tools.name: kb_delete_agent_profile
tools.description: Delete the profile for an agent by its agent_id. Returns deleted=true if the profile existed and was removed, deleted=false if not found.

agent_id.description: Unique identifier for the agent whose profile should be deleted.

tools.name: kb_remember_preview
tools.description: Dry-run a memory write before calling kb_remember. It searches nearby memories in the target brain bucket, returns duplicate candidates, possible contradiction warnings, the structured metadata that would be written, and a legacy recommendation: create, update, merge, or ask_user. The structured relationship and recommended_action fields explain the safe next step; a targetless related write recommends create because this tool never selects a neighbour as an update target. This tool never writes, deletes, or updates memory.

text.description: The memory text to preview. Use the exact text you would pass to kb_remember.

share_level.description: Explicit memory tier. Omit for the conservative 'user' default.

source.description: Optional provenance tag. Included only in the preview metadata/source decision.

memory_type.description: Structured memory kind. Defaults from type.

context_scope.description: Context scope. Episodic/reflective data is Agent-private by default; shared working context is blocked unless collaboration is explicit.

collaboration_members.description: Explicit bounded Agent membership for a collaboration note; the current server-derived Agent must be included.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO datetime after which this memory should be treated as stale.

staleness_hint_days.description: Optional age hint for Memory Health.

supersedes.description: Optional memory_id/item-id list this memory supersedes.

event.description: Structured recent-activity contract. Presence stores this memory as episodic/Event. Fields are optional for backward compatibility; event_id enables strongest retry dedup.

tools.name: kb_remember
tools.description:
Save a memory the agent should keep across sessions. CALL THIS whenever you learn something worth remembering: a user preference ('I prefer X over Y'), a project fact ('this repo uses Postgres + pgvector'), a non-obvious decision ('we picked BGE because of cost'), or a useful skill you just discovered.

`type` selects which memory bucket the fact lands in:
  - 'semantic'   (default) stable facts, preferences, conventions
  - 'episodic'   things that happened, conversation events, dated occurrences
  - 'procedural' how-to knowledge, code snippets, runbooks, prompt templates
  - 'reflective' synthesized insights you wrote yourself after thinking about other memories

`importance` is 1-10 (default 5). Use 8-10 for things you must not forget (strong preferences, security constraints), 1-3 for trivia.

The tool runs the same preview automatically. Related memories allow create; updates require an explicit target: the targetless write uses the structured `recommended_action=create` and never selects or overwrites a neighbour. Safe create recommendations write in one tool call; likely duplicates (`merge`) or contradictions (`ask_user`) return MEMORY_PREVIEW_REQUIRED without writing. Retry with `force:true` only after an explicit decision; forced writes carry a durable metadata audit record. Use `kb_update_memory` for an explicit target update.

text.description: The memory itself, in natural language. Write a complete sentence — short fragments retrieve poorly. The first non-blank line becomes the title (≤120 chars).

type.description: Memory bucket (default 'semantic'). See tool description for when to pick each.

share_level.description: Explicit memory tier. Omit for the conservative 'user' default; a higher tier is never inferred.

importance.description: Importance 1-10 (default 5). Influences recall ranking — important memories surface first when other signals tie.

memory_type.description: Structured memory kind. Defaults from type: semantic=Fact, episodic=Event, procedural=Runbook, reflective=Insight.

project.description: Project or domain this memory belongs to. Default 'general'. Examples: 'KB-API', 'Globe3'.

confidence.description: Evidence confidence. Default 'unverified'; use 'verified' only when grounded in code, docs, or user confirmation.

source_kind.description: Where the memory came from. Default 'user'. Use 'code', 'docs', 'user', or 'inference'.

context_scope.description: Context scope. Agent-private is the default for working/experience memories. Collaboration requires an explicit id and membership list.

collaboration_members.description: Explicit bounded Agent membership for a collaboration note; the current server-derived Agent must be included.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO datetime after which this memory should be treated as stale.

staleness_hint_days.description: Optional age hint. Memory Health flags the item when updated_at is older than this many days.

supersedes.description: Optional memory_id/item-id list this memory supersedes. Stored in metadata for review.

force.description: Explicitly bypass a `merge` or `ask_user` preview recommendation. Omit by default; forced writes are audited in item metadata.

idempotency_key.description: Stable identity for one logical memory write. Generate once, then reuse the exact same value only when retrying after timeout/502 or an unknown outcome.

event.description: Structured recent-activity contract. Presence stores this memory as episodic/Event. Fields are optional for backward compatibility; event_id enables strongest retry dedup.

tools.name: kb_recall
tools.description:
Retrieve memories relevant to a query. CALL THIS at the START of any non-trivial task to load prior context (user preferences, past decisions, project facts, learned skills) — your context window does not persist across sessions, but kb_recall does.

Use full-sentence queries that mirror how the memory might have been written ('what does the user prefer for embeddings?' beats 'embeddings'). The search is semantic, not keyword — phrasing matters.

Returns ranked memories with `blended_score` combining similarity + importance + recency. Within 0.10 of the best hit (KB_MCP_RECALL_SIM_BAND), preserve backend order and allow each candidate at most one adjacent exchange using that blend, before identifier filtering and canonical grouping. Below the band the order is pure similarity, so a high-importance memory can never bury a much stronger match. Memories with similarity < 0.4 are filtered out; if `results` is empty the brain genuinely has nothing — say so to the user, do not invent. Treat < 0.4 as probable noise, but calibrate against the active model — high-band models (bge-m3, e5) score even unrelated content 0.6–0.8, so verify content rather than trusting scores. When the query names a specific identifier/marker, a candidate must literally contain it to be returned at all (pure embedding similarity to unrelated text is not enough) — this is why a deleted or nonexistent marker correctly comes back empty. `confident:false` plus a `note` means treat `results` as a loose lead, not a confirmed memory.

Distinct memory IDs retain their provenance; returned excerpts of the same memory are combined before the result limit. Query similarity alone never triggers a consolidation hint. Review the original memories before explicitly requesting kb_merge.

query.description: Natural-language query. Full sentences work much better than keywords.

k.description: Max memories to return after dedup (default 8, max 50).

types.description: Restrict to specific memory buckets (e.g. ['semantic','procedural']). Omit to search all four.

tools.name: kb_update_memory
tools.description: Preview a safe update of an existing memory's text, provenance, or structured metadata. This tool never mutates memory; it returns a lifecycle plan. Review the plan and pass its plan_id plus explicit action_ids to kb_bulk_manage. Text changes are re-embedded when applied.

memory_id.description: Opaque memory_id from a previous kb_remember or kb_recall response.

new_text.description: Full replacement text. The first non-blank line becomes the new title.

source.description: Replace provenance source; pass null to clear.

metadata.description: Additional metadata fields to merge during lifecycle apply.

protected.description: Set or clear the protected-memory guard. Protected records cannot be destructively managed.

tools.name: kb_forget
tools.description: Preview permanent deletion of one memory. This tool never deletes immediately: it returns a protected lifecycle plan. Prefer kb_archive when recovery may be needed. Review the plan, then use kb_bulk_manage with explicit action_ids and dry_run=true before real apply.

memory_id.description: Opaque memory_id from a previous kb_remember or kb_recall response.

tools.name: kb_merge
tools.description:
Preview consolidation of 2+ overlapping memories into one canonical memory. This tool never merges or archives immediately; it infers the target Brain bucket and returns a lifecycle plan for review.

Workflow: read the candidates (you already have their text from kb_recall), write ONE concise summary that captures their union, call kb_merge, then apply the reviewed action ids through kb_bulk_manage. The canonical memory carries provenance, the highest importance among the inputs, and the most common type among the inputs (unless you override `type`). All sources must resolve to that same Brain type bucket so the supersession graph remains self-contained and exportable.

Do NOT merge memories that genuinely differ (e.g. two distinct preferences for two different projects) — `kb_keep_both` doesn't exist; the right move is to leave them alone.

memory_ids.description: At least 2 memory_ids to consolidate (from kb_recall). Sources are handled by the lifecycle plan.

summary.description: Your consolidated statement that supersedes all inputs. Becomes the new memory's text.

type.description: Override the target bucket. Default: most common brain_type among inputs.

importance.description: Override importance. Default: max importance among inputs.

tools.name: kb_summarize_topic
tools.description:
Pull a wide slice of memories about a topic so YOU can synthesize them into a higher-level insight. CALL THIS when the user asks 'what have you learned about X?', 'summarize what we know about Y', or when you notice you've recalled many overlapping memories about the same theme and want to consolidate them.

Returns the raw memories grouped by type (episodic / semantic / procedural / reflective) along with a `hint` telling you exactly what to do next — typically: (a) write a 1-3 sentence synthesis, (b) save it via kb_remember(text=…, type='reflective'), and optionally (c) kb_merge the originals if they are now redundant. This is how the brain gets smarter over time without any backend LLM or background worker — YOU are the reflection engine.

query.description: Topic / theme to gather memories about. Phrase it the way the memories were written.

k.description: How many memories to pull (default 30, max 50). Use higher for broader synthesis.

tools.name: kb_graph_answer
tools.description: Answer an engineering question with bounded semantic retrieval plus confirmed, evidenced graph context. The server refuses unsupported or private/conditional external context and returns no_answer with gaps when the evidence is insufficient. Prefer this for answer-like GraphRAG requests; citations include stable source references and content-free graph paths.

query.description: Question to answer from the KB and verified graph

expand_relations.description: Optional uppercase edge allowlist; omit to follow all non-bookkeeping edges

tools.name: kb_add_relation
tools.description: Create a typed edge between two knowledge items. By default both items must be in the same KB; set cross_kb=true to allow dst_id from another visible KB while src_id stays in kb_id. Prefer relation_type (semantic enum) over edge_type (legacy UPPERCASE). Call kb_list_relations first to avoid creating duplicate edges. Idempotent: re-adding an existing (src_id, dst_id, edge_type) triplet returns the existing row.

kb_id.description: Source knowledge base uuid. src_id must belong to this KB.

relation_type.description: Standard semantic relation (preferred). supports=A reinforces B; contradicts=A negates B; extends=A builds on B; compares=A benchmarks B; reuses=A incorporates B; adapts=A modifies B for new context; criticizes=A finds weaknesses in B; generalizes=A abstracts over B; modifies=A patches B. Takes precedence over edge_type when both are supplied.

edge_type.description: Legacy free-form edge type: uppercase letters/digits/underscore, max 32 chars (e.g. CITES, MENTIONS, SUPERSEDES, HAS_CHUNK). Use relation_type instead when possible.

props.description: Optional free-form JSON metadata for this edge

cross_kb.description: Allow dst_id to belong to another KB visible to the caller. Default false keeps same-KB behavior.

tools.name: kb_list_relations
tools.description: List typed edges in a KB, optionally filtered by src_id, dst_id, or edge_type. Call this before kb_add_relation to check whether an edge already exists, or to inspect the graph structure of a specific item.

src_id.description: Filter: only edges starting from this item

dst_id.description: Filter: only edges pointing to this item

edge_type.description: Filter: only edges of this legacy UPPERCASE type

relation_type.description: Filter: only edges of this standard semantic type. Alias for edge_type — normalized server-side so it matches relations however they were created.

tools.name: kb_delete_relation
tools.description: Delete one exact typed edge between two knowledge items — the correction path when kb_add_relation created a wrong or stale link. Requires an exact (src_id, dst_id, edge_type) match; use kb_list_relations first if you're not sure of the exact type. Idempotent: deleting an edge that no longer exists returns deleted:false rather than an error, so it's safe to retry. Deleting only removes the edge — both items are untouched.

kb_id.description: Knowledge base uuid that src_id belongs to (same kb_id used in kb_add_relation).

relation_type.description: Standard semantic relation to delete (preferred). Takes precedence over edge_type when both are supplied.

edge_type.description: Legacy UPPERCASE edge type to delete (e.g. CITES, MENTIONS). Use relation_type instead when possible.

tools.name: kb_expand_neighbors
tools.description: Starting from a set of seed item ids (e.g. top hits from kb_search), traverse the knowledge graph and return connected neighbor items. Use after kb_search to pull cross-document context. depth>1 grows results fast — start with hops=1. Neighbors carry via_graph:true, a depth-decay score (0.5/depth), and, when available, graph_seed_id plus an ordered graph_path of content-free edge metadata for deterministic attribution.

seed_ids.description: Item ids to expand from (use item.id from kb_search results)

hops.description: Max traversal depth 1–3 (default 1). Each hop can multiply result count.

citation_type.description: Shorthand: restrict traversal to one standard semantic relation type. Merged with edge_types when both are provided. e.g. citation_type='extends' follows only 'extends' edges.

edge_types.description: Restrict traversal to these legacy UPPERCASE edge types. Omit to follow all types.

directed.description: When true, follow only outgoing edges (src→dst). Default false (undirected).

tools.name: kb_citation_lineage
tools.description: Trace a directed citation/derivation chain from a single seed item. Returns an ordered list of ancestor (or descendant) items hop-by-hop, each labelled with the relation type and content-free edge/path metadata used to reach it. Use 'ancestors' direction to answer 'what did this item build on / extend / reuse?' Use 'descendants' direction to answer 'what has built on this item since?'. More precise than kb_expand_neighbors for single-root lineage queries — this tool follows a directed path, not a star-shaped graph expansion.

relation_types.description: Edge types to follow. Default: ["extends","reuses","adapts"]. Include other RelationType values (supports, compares, …) or legacy UPPERCASE types as needed.

max_depth.description: Maximum hops to traverse (default 5, max 10). Each hop follows one edge.

direction.description: ancestors (default): follow src→dst — 'what did this item build on?'. descendants: follow dst→src — 'what has built on this item?'.

tools.name: kb_gap_detection
tools.description: Analyse the entity_type coverage of a knowledge base and surface knowledge gaps. Returns which categories are well-populated (covered), thin (sparse), or completely absent (missing). Use before an ingestion session to direct the agent toward under-represented topics. If the KB has schema_type set (scientific/enterprise/legal/technical), the server automatically uses that schema's vocabulary as the reference list — no need to supply reference_types manually. Returns: total_items, uncategorized (no entity_type), covered (≥ min_count), sparse (< min_count), missing (zero items), and schema_type (the KB's schema if set).

reference_types.description: Entity types to check for gaps. Omit to auto-detect: if the KB has schema_type set, its vocabulary is used; otherwise falls back to the full standard vocabulary (fact, concept, event, person, organization, product, motivation, hypothesis, finding, limitation, method, dataset, process, module, error_condition, solution, configuration, rule, api_endpoint, code_pattern, bug, fix, dependency, deployment). Supply an explicit list to scope the check to a subset.

min_count.description: Minimum item count for a type to be considered 'covered'. Types below this are 'sparse'. Default 3.

instructions:
Knowledge Builder API — SIX interfaces:

1. DEFAULT AGENT BRAIN: use kb_brain_remember, kb_brain_recall, kb_brain_update, kb_brain_forget, kb_brain_context, and kb_brain_status for ordinary persistent-memory workflows. These six facade tools safely orchestrate the existing Brain, lifecycle, retrieval, profile, routing, and health infrastructure; needs_review is a normal zero-write result. Use kb_brain_belief_resolve explicitly for the read-only current-belief projection; it is not a legacy recall or serving switch. Use kb_brain_whoami when identity, profile, scope, or Brain bucket availability is unclear; it is read-only and secret-free.

ADVANCED BRAIN tools: kb_bootstrap, kb_context_for_message, kb_remember, kb_recall, kb_remember_preview, kb_update_memory, kb_forget, kb_merge, kb_archive, kb_bulk_manage, kb_summarize_topic, kb_memory_health, kb_confidence_reconciliation_report, kb_set_agent_profile, kb_get_agent_profile, kb_list_agent_profiles, kb_delete_agent_profile. Use these as your long-term memory across sessions — they auto-manage four hidden KBs (episodic / semantic / procedural / reflective) and return opaque memory_id strings. At the START of any non-trivial task, call kb_recall to load relevant prior context. Memory update/delete/merge/archive tools return preview plans only; review them, then use kb_bulk_manage with the plan_id and explicit action_ids. Apply defaults to dry-run. After learning anything worth keeping (user preferences, project facts, useful skills, debugging insights), call kb_remember.

2. CRUD tools (operator/admin work): kb_list, kb_create, kb_get, kb_update, kb_delete, kb_list_items, kb_get_item, kb_open_section, kb_list_pdf_outline, kb_open_pdf_outline_node, kb_list_pdf_tagged_structure, kb_open_pdf_tagged_candidate, kb_begin_structure_navigation, kb_complete_structure_navigation, kb_add_item, kb_ingest_document, kb_bulk_add_item, kb_update_item, kb_delete_item, kb_search, kb_retrieve, kb_search_all, kb_find_similar, kb_answer, kb_optimize_analyze, kb_optimize_apply. Use these to manage user-facing KBs (documentation, ingested docs, etc.) — NOT for the agent's own memory. Pick by intent: kb_add_item = one short item; kb_ingest_document = one long document (auto-split into chunks); kb_bulk_add_item = many short items in one call. For answer-like retrieval inside a known KB, prefer kb_answer first: it returns a citation-ready context pack (rerank + parent-merge + graph neighbours) in one call. Use kb_search only when you intentionally need raw ranked hits for inspection, debugging, or a custom workflow. Use kb_retrieve when one bounded search may be weak: it preserves explicit scope and hard constraints while trying at most three distinct strategies; BM25 remains a specialist fallback and the default Hybrid route is unchanged. After using a kb_answer/kb_search/kb_retrieve/kb_search_all result, you may call kb_feedback(search_event_id, helpful) to record whether the retrieval actually answered the question — this trains the Answer-accuracy analytics. For PROOF-OF-ORIGIN, kb_get_item_provenance lists the source document/page/region + proof-image size of an imported item, and kb_get_source_image returns bounded proof-image metadata and an authenticated source URL, plus an image block when the response budget permits, to show an end user where a fact came from. For a cited selectable PDF with native bookmarks, kb_list_pdf_outline then kb_open_pdf_outline_node provide explicit, bounded page-local navigation. For exact native Table/TR rows and internal XYZ references, use kb_list_pdf_tagged_structure then kb_open_pdf_tagged_candidate; target locators are never auto-followed. These navigation reads never invoke an LLM Provider.

Structure Navigation V1 is Search-bound and fail-closed: (1) call kb_search, kb_answer, or kb_search_all first; (2) create kb_begin_structure_navigation only when a trusted returned citation needs surrounding, table, section, or linked evidence; (3) pass only server-returned node/candidate ids and the required navigation_session_id; (4) reference targets are locators only and are never auto-followed; (5) STRUCTURE_UNAVAILABLE, citation/hash mismatch, expired session, or NAVIGATION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED means stop and return insufficient_evidence; (6) the Agent performs reasoning/composition and calls kb_complete_structure_navigation, while KB-API never generates an answer or calls an external LLM.

3. GRAPH tools (knowledge graph): kb_graph_answer, kb_add_relation, kb_list_relations, kb_delete_relation, kb_expand_neighbors, kb_citation_lineage, kb_gap_detection. Use kb_graph_answer for evidence-grounded answers; use the lower-level tools to inspect or edit graph structure. Pattern: kb_search → kb_expand_neighbors (using hit item ids as seed_ids) → broader context.

4. TOOL REGISTRY tools (agent productivity): kb_tool_search, kb_tool_get, kb_tool_register, kb_tool_test, and kb_tool_run manage approved tool definitions stored as normal KB items with kbcid='agent.tool' and metadata.kind='tool'. These tools return and validate contracts, schemas, artifacts, safety metadata, harness metadata, and provenance so the agent can choose the right tool. kb_tool_run executes read_only HTTP GET artifacts against the configured KB_API_BASE origin, plus read_only shell/node artifacts inside a bounded worker process. Pre-approved writes_local Node tools can run inside an isolated output directory with manifest, verification, and cleanup metadata. Other non-read-only tools stay dry-run only. Python/sql artifacts remain discovery-only.

5. RSI tools: kb_rsi_status, kb_rsi_failures, kb_rsi_candidates, kb_rsi_candidate_history, kb_rsi_candidate_compare are tenant-readable inspection tools. Master-only control tools kb_rsi_control_status, kb_rsi_propose, kb_rsi_experiment, kb_rsi_pause, kb_rsi_resume, kb_rsi_promote, kb_rsi_rollback, and root-only kb_rsi_policy expose the explicit control plane. The API enforces scope, fingerprints, consent, append-only audit, and fail-closed promotion; none of these tools expose raw query/item content or activate serving changes.

6. ENGINEERING REUSE tools (mandatory before meaningful implementation): kb_reuse_context returns a cross-project Reuse Pack with independent capabilities, Skills, procedural Brain memory, project prior art, pitfalls, security/QA invariants, provenance, applicability, gate status, and search-event telemetry. Use kb_reuse_feedback after implementation to record usefulness and selected prior art. Use kb_reuse_lesson_propose only to prepare a provenance-backed, independently verified lesson/Skill packet for owner review; it never writes or auto-promotes anything. Small UI/copy edits are exempt; a genuine no-prior-art result explicitly permits fresh research.

Scores on search hits are cosine similarity in [0, 1]. Treat < 0.4 as probable noise, but calibrate against the active model — high-band models (bge-m3, e5) score even unrelated content 0.6–0.8, so verify content rather than trusting scores.
